steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Functionalist view: education serves vital functions for society. Durkheim: education transmits society's norms and values (social solidarity) and teaches specialist skills for the division of labour. Parsons: education is the main agent of secondary socialisation and a bridge between family and wider society; it promotes meritocracy (everyone has equal opportunity to succeed based on ability and effort). | Key Fact: Marxist view: education serves capitalism. Althusser: education is an Ideological State Apparatus (ISA) that transmits ruling class ideology, making inequality seem natural and inevitable. Bowles and Gintis: the correspondence principle - schools mirror the workplace through the hidden curriculum (hierarchy, competition, obedience to authority, punctuality) preparing

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Compare Functionalist and Marxist views of the role of education. | Explain what the hidden curriculum is and evaluate its importance in education. | Evaluate whether the education system is meritocratic.
